clue.text: Wretched play entertains British setter in Caen

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside your home, so one part holds the others

blocks.note: a play is an act on stage, here split around the guests
B is the standard abbreviation for British
the setter says 'I', and in French, spoken in Caen, that is je

explanation.surface: A miserable stage production features a British crossword compiler living in Normandy.
explanation.walkthrough: Caen is a city in Normandy, so the setter's 'I' must be put into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject describes a state of utter misery or degradation, a close synonym for wretched.

clue.text: Wood from area below raised flag

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word turns it so it reads from the bottom upwards
in a down entry, a piece placed below another simply follows it

blocks.note: a flag is a flat paving stone, a slab
A is the usual abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Something wooden appears under a banner that has been hoisted up a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' pretends to be a banner; it is a flagstone. A flagstone reversed sits above the area letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber from a tropical American tree, popular for model-making.

clue.text: Poor Angles penning verse during subjugation

indicators.note: something in poor shape has fallen apart, so its letters are rearranged
penning means shutting something in an enclosure, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: the six letters of this word are mixed up
V is the abbreviation for verse
during a period is in it

explanation.surface: The unfortunate Angles were made to write poetry while under conquest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angles were a Germanic people who settled in England; here they are only letters. ENSLAG holds V and IN to give ENSLAVING.
explanation.definitionFit: Enslaving, used as a noun, is the act of reducing people to subjection, which is subjugation.

clue.text: Somersaulting routine at top of program for swimmer

indicators.note: a somersault turns a body head over heels, so the word is flipped end to end
in a down entry, a piece at the top of another comes first

blocks.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine
a bot is an automated computer program

explanation.surface: A gymnastic routine tops the bill of a show designed for a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' is a crossword favourite for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large flatfish, and any fish is a swimmer in crossword language.

clue.text: Old man in retirement with little desire

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
petite means small or little

explanation.surface: A retired father now wants very little out of life.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite is a craving or longing for something, a synonym of desire.

clue.text: Drugs colonists smuggling fish and iron south

indicators.note: smuggled goods are hidden inside something, so the next letters go within

blocks.note: ants live in colonies; the plural gives two of them
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular
to iron clothes is to press them
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Settlers are caught hiding drugs inside fish and metal shipped south.
explanation.walkthrough: One colonist ant stands on each side of the smuggled IDE and PRESS, then S ends it: ANT-IDE-PRESS-ANT-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Antidepressants are a class of medicines prescribed for depression, so they are drugs.

clue.text: City spa a Dane transformed

indicators.note: something transformed has changed its form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these three words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian visitor turns a health resort into a whole city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasadena is a city in Los Angeles County, California, home of the Rose Bowl.

clue.text: Piano used only once in best film theme

indicators.note: using a letter only once means one of its two copies is dropped where the pieces meet

blocks.note: top means best, as in top marks
pic is informal for a film or picture
P, piano in music, appears at the join of the two pieces and is written once

explanation.surface: In a prize-winning movie's theme tune, the piano is heard only once.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces share a P where they meet, and the clue tells you to write it only once.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject or theme of discussion or writing.

clue.text: Recalled rubbish guide for one who interrogates?

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is taken back to front

blocks.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
a mentor is a trusted guide or adviser

explanation.surface: A rubbish guide is brought back in to question someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: an interrogator may well torment.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh interrogator inflicts distress, so may be described as a tormentor, a definition by example.

clue.text: Female bears worn-out in ceremonies at the end?

indicators.note: to bear something is to carry it, so the girl carries the next word inside

blocks.note: a lass is a girl or young woman
trite means hackneyed, worn-out through overuse

explanation.surface: A woman feels exhausted at the close of long ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a cryptic definition: these rites come at the end of life, not of a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: The last rites are the sacraments given to a dying person, ceremonies performed at life's close.

clue.text: Bonus and a fine Oscar rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a, as in 'ten pounds a head', means per
OK means fine, all right
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An award-winner turns down a generous payout and a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' looks like the film award; it is the radio-alphabet letter O, which is dropped from OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk is a fringe benefit or extra on top of pay, a bonus.

clue.text: Unsettled agent on centre of driving range

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its single middle letter
in an across entry, one piece on another follows after it

blocks.note: the fourth of seven letters sits at the centre
an Aga is a brand of heavy cast-iron cooking range found in British country kitchens
James Bond is the famous fictional secret agent

explanation.surface: A restless spy takes a turn at the golf driving range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving range' reads as one golfing phrase, but it splits: a letter from 'driving' and a cooker for 'range'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagabond is a wanderer without a home, so the word works as an adjective meaning rootless or unsettled.

clue.text: Order from bank almost at the end of month

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
placing one piece at the end of another means it follows on after it

blocks.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
a reef is a ridge or bank of rock or sand near the sea surface

explanation.surface: A banking instruction is issued nearly at the close of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money; it is a sandbank or reef.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order issued by an authority such as a ruler or court.

clue.text: Shaving sides of composer's tongue

indicators.note: shaving the sides trims both edges, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: Frédéric Chopin, the Polish composer

explanation.surface: Shaving off a composer's sideburns reveals his tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' sounds anatomical next to 'composer's'; it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopi is the Uto-Aztecan language of the Hopi people of Arizona, and a tongue is a language.

clue.text: 'Zero' variety dandies periodically drink

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every second letter is kept

blocks.note: zero looks like the letter O
a range is a variety or assortment
the second, fourth and sixth letters are kept

explanation.surface: Fashionable dandies sip a 'zero' version of their usual tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zero' in quotes hints at a sugar-free drink, but it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured with orange.

clue.text: Mines trapping last of ten decrepit river vessels

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so these letters go within
the last of a word is its final letter, taken from each of the next two words

blocks.note: a pit is a coal mine
the final letter of this word
the final letter of this word
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Old mines have swallowed ten broken-down river boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests boats with the river; these vessels are drinking mugs. 'Last of' serves both ten and decrepit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pint pots are tankards holding a pint of beer, and a drinking container is a vessel.

clue.text: Wide slate I see beneath old stuff

indicators.note: in a down entry, what lies beneath comes later in the answer

blocks.note: to slate or pan something is to criticise it harshly
O is the abbreviation for old
to stuff is to cram or ram in
I as written, and the letter C pronounced the same as see

explanation.surface: A broad roof of slate is spotted underneath a heap of old belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slate' looks like roofing; it is the verb meaning criticise. The pieces go PAN, O, RAM, then I and C at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Panoramic means giving a wide, sweeping view of a whole area.

clue.text: Luxury seeker enthralled by classy bar items

indicators.note: something enthralled is held captive, so the answer is held within the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone who loves the good life is captivated by the posh offerings at a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite, named after the pleasure-loving citizens of ancient Sybaris, devotes life to luxury and pleasure.

clue.text: Carving of grand ship English city returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read in the reverse direction

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: A sculpture of a great ship is sent back to an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a grotesque carved figure, often a waterspout, on a church or cathedral.

clue.text: Standard response Mary and Joseph received?

blocks.note: first meaning: the usual level or pattern
second meaning, cryptic: at Bethlehem the innkeeper said there was no room, abbreviated in the way a small ad shortens room to rm

explanation.walkthrough: The Nativity story has the couple told there was no room at the inn; written in shorthand that reply runs NO RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the accepted standard of behaviour or the typical level, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Wind hammered pair invading isle needing cover

indicators.note: something hammered is beaten out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
a word that needs a cover has lost its outer layer, leaving only its inner letters
to invade is to go inside territory, so these letters enter the other piece

blocks.note: these four letters are rearranged
the two inner letters are kept

explanation.surface: A battered couple land on an exposed island buffeted by the wind, looking for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as the weather, but the definition is the verb, to wind round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: To spiral is to wind or twist in a continuous curve, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Article 1.8 about reptile

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, as in about-face, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
read as a date, day 1 of month 8 is the first of August: AUG and I, Roman one

explanation.surface: A legal article numbered 1.8 concerns a lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: '1.8' looks like a section number or decimal; read as a British-style date it is 1 August.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard, and lizards are reptiles.

clue.text: Note turned up behind Book of Memories

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning a word upwards means reading it from the bottom
a word placed behind another comes after it in the answer

blocks.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
bum is British slang for the behind, the buttocks

explanation.surface: A note appears tucked behind a volume of reminiscences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' does double duty: it places the second piece after the first and supplies that piece itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a blank book for keeping photographs and souvenirs, a book of memories.

clue.text: Individual component houses key within clock

indicators.note: a house holds people inside, so the next letter goes within
within places the whole thing inside the next word

blocks.note: to clock someone is British slang for to notice or see them
a part is a component
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A single machine component contains the key that fits inside a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' looks like a timepiece; it is the slang verb meaning spot, and it holds everything else. 'Within' nests the second container inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate means distinct and standing apart, so it can stand for individual as an adjective.

clue.text: Bit of refuse making wife tense

indicators.note: making one thing into another means one letter is turned into a different one

blocks.note: refuse is rubbish, waste
W is the abbreviation for wife
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A scrap of rubbish leaves a spouse stressed and on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as nervous, but it is the grammar abbreviation that replaces the wife letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste is a small sample or morsel of food, a little bit.

clue.text: Dig west half of island

indicators.note: in an across entry the west is the left, so only the left-hand half is kept

blocks.note: Barbuda is a Caribbean island, part of Antigua and Barbuda

explanation.surface: An excavation is planned on the western side of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Seven letters have no exact half; the first four, before the U, are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A dig is a cutting remark, and so is a barb, a pointed insult.

clue.text: Fool exposed Italians in front of two Americans

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of covering, so the outer letters come off
in front of means this piece comes first, before the others

blocks.note: signori is Italian for gentlemen, the plural of signor
AM for American and US, two abbreviations for American

explanation.surface: An idiot exposes a group of Italians to a couple of American tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant or stupid person, close in sense to a fool.

clue.text: Flowing water joins lake in state

indicators.note: joining puts one piece directly against the next
in places one letter inside the following word

blocks.note: the sea is a body of water
a state of disorder is a mess, as in 'what a state'
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Running water flows into a lake inside a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a US state; it is a mess. The lake letter slips in after the M: SEA + M-L-ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamless prose or movement is smooth and continuous, without breaks, so it is flowing.

clue.text: A lot of fabric pinned to leading footman?

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes
pinned to means fixed beside, so the pieces join end to end

blocks.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
key means leading or principal, as in a key player

explanation.surface: Much of the fabric is pinned to the uniform of a senior footman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: a footman is one kind of lackey.
explanation.definitionFit: A lackey is a liveried servant or menial attendant, and a footman is one such servant.
